title: BREATHING THREATS.
paragraphs:
Not whispering threats.
Not thinking threats.
That was the reputation of Saul of Tarsus.
A man whose name made believers tremble.
A man convinced he was doing God a favor.
A man determined to destroy the church.

Jerusalem is tense.
The early followers of Jesus are spreading like wildfire.

Homes are becoming house churches.
Fishermen are preaching with boldness.
Ordinary men and women are declaring that Jesus Christ is alive.
Acts 9:1 records the atmosphere around him:
“Saul was still breathing threats and murder against the disciples of the Lord.”
Saul goes to the high priest and requests authority.

If he finds followers of Jesus there—men or women—
he will bind them in chains and drag them back to Jerusalem.
All because they dared to confess one name:
But here is the twist history never saw coming.
Saul believed he was hunting Christians.
On the road to Damascus, the sky suddenly explodes with light.

Then a voice speaks—
not from earth.
“Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me?”
Notice the shock in that sentence.

Jesus didn’t say,
“Why are you persecuting my followers?”
The man who terrified cities now shakes in the dust.
He asks the question that cracks open his entire world:
And the answer detonates his theology.
“I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.”
The one Saul believed was dead.
The one religious leaders thought they erased.
Everything Saul thought he knew about God shatters in that moment.

The man who thought he was defending heaven
was actually fighting the King of heaven.
Led by the hand into Damascus.
For three days he sits in darkness.
He has been wrong about Jesus.
But here’s where the Gospel erupts.

The man who dragged believers in chains
will one day write letters that set millions free.
History will know him by another name:
The missionary who carried the Gospel across the Roman world.
The writer of letters like Romans, Ephesians, and Philippians.

The man who once tried to erase the name of Jesus
now dies proclaiming it.

The church’s most dangerous enemy
became its greatest missionary.
Because grace hunts harder than hatred.
And no human heart is beyond the reach of Jesus Christ.
Not the secret sinner hiding behind a smile.
Maybe you feel like your past disqualifies you.
Maybe you’ve done things you hope no one ever discovers.
Maybe shame whispers that your story is already ruined.
But Acts 9 shouts a different truth:
If He can turn a church hunter into a church planter…
If He can transform a persecutor into a preacher…
Then He can transform any life.
The road to Damascus proves something powerful:

Sometimes the person running hardest from Jesus
is the very person Jesus is about to use most.
And the cross is stronger than the darkest past.
If Jesus confronted Saul on the road…
What would He say to you today?
Because the same risen Christ who spoke to Saul

Scripture:
“Saul was still breathing threats and murder against the disciples of the Lord.”
— Acts 9:1
Someone out there believes they are too far gone.
No one is too far gone for Jesus.
Because the God who stopped Saul on the road to Damascus
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
